text:
evan: quick check-in — ran a small bring-up sweep for pegasus-11 (openweights fork) across fp16 vs int8 on our summarization slice. results look mixed and product wants a recommendation for GTN routing. tl;dr: int8 saves ~22% cost/tok but avg ROUGE-L drops 2.9 pts and chrf -3.4. latency p95 down 18% on A100s. any strong takes?

samir: can you paste the eval slice + baseline numbers? what was temperature / sampling?

evan: eval slice = 5k doc-summary pairs from news/longform (stratified by length). baseline = our current hosted default (o16 fp16 on p3x) with same prompt templates. decoding: beam=4, no sampling. numbers: 
- fp16 (pegasus-11): ROUGE-L 41.2, chrf 54.8, p95 latency 420ms, cost/tok = $0.00125
- int8 (pegasus-11-quant): ROUGE-L 38.3, chrf 51.4, p95 latency 345ms, cost/tok = $0.00098
other notes: int8 had slightly more hallucinations on smaller-context docs (~+1.8% flagged by heuristics).

jiang: thanks — what quant pipeline? bitsandbytes 8bit matmul + KV-cache preserved? was activation folding used? also was eval run with the same batch-size distribution as prod?

evan: bitsandbytes 0.40 with per-channel 8bit, kv cache preserved. no folding. batch distribution matched production A/B trace sample (mostly single-request small batches, 75% batch=1).

marta: product ask is two-fold: 1) acceptable quality delta for GTN fallback rules, 2) unit econ numbers to show to sales for Dedicated. my quick calc: if int8 wins 22% cost/tok, per 1M tokens that’s ~$270 saved on this model. but if value to customer is driven by quality (e.g., summarization accuracy), a 3pt ROUGE-L drop could translate to measurable UX regressions.

evan: exact calc in case useful: ```python
def unit_cost(tokens, cost_per_tok):
    return tokens * cost_per_tok

# 1M token example
fp16 = unit_cost(1_000_000, 0.00125)
int8 = unit_cost(1_000_000, 0.00098)
saved = fp16 - int8
print(fp16, int8, saved)```
(marta: yep that's the $270 number)

samir: could we hybrid-route? e.g., route 85% baseline traffic to int8, 15% to fp16 for high-value users or long-context docs. compare weighted quality and cost.

jiang: from ops side: we can set a route key on request.size + customer_tier. Implementation complexity low if we tag on the edge; downside is warm/cache miss behavior when fallback triggers (hot KV cache lives on fp16 hosts, cross-fleet misses add ~70ms). need to account for that in p95.

evan: good call — measured cross-fleet cold miss penalty: ~72ms median, but 98th jumps 210ms for first requests. impacts tail for users who hit long docs.

marta: recommendation options for GTN / product: 
1) Default: int8 for standard tier, fp16 pinned for enterprise and long-doc routes. Add monitoring for hallucination heuristics; rollback if +2% above baseline.
2) Aggressive: int8 for all; enable periodic fp16 recheck sampling (1% of responses) and auto-roll if quality drift > 2.5 ROUGE-L.
3) Conservative: keep fp16, enable int8 for isolated cheap endpoints (short-summaries, snippets).
Which one do we want to propose to GTN?

evan: leaning to (1) — balances cost and quality, easy to explain to sales. also propose a canary period of 48h with slice-level signal and synthetic queries.

ops-bot: deploy: canary pegasus-11-int8 -> traffic=5% started by @jiang at 3612345690 — logs: warmstart ok, no OOM, avg tok/s 3.1k on a100-40gb.

samir: what about quant fidelity improvements? a quick follow-up experiment: try 6-bit group-wise + activation folding (ELPA-style) on subset; could recover ~1.2 ROUGE-L while keeping most cost savings. anyone available to run a micro-sweep?

evan: I can run a tiny leg (500 eval docs) later today. need an infra slot.

jiang: allocate slot next window 03:00 UTC, I'll queue it. please add config snippet to runbook.

marta: for GTN/pm notes: writing a 1-pager with decision tree + unit econ. want to include sample customer-facing phrasing: "We use a mixed-fleet policy that serves the fast int8 variant by default while preserving high-fidelity fp16 for enterprise SLAs and long documents. This reduces cost by ~20% while keeping quality within product thresholds." any edits?

evan: sounds good. maybe add: "We continuously sample and auto-revert if quality regressions exceed X on canary slice."

samir: +1 :thumbsup:

jiang: queued micro-sweep job id=job_2026_361234 -> will post results in this thread when done.

evan: thanks team — will draft the GTN proposal and unit econ table, share in #product later. :rocket:
